thread.title: House passes Carter-led bill to extend rural health care programs
thread.title_full: House passes Carter-led bill to extend rural health care programs

author: T. A. Sweeney
title: House passes Carter-led bill to extend rural health care programs
text:
Rep. Earl L. “Buddy” Carter announced on Apr. 22 that the House of Representatives passed the Improving Care in Rural America Reauthorization Act of 2025, a bill aimed at extending programs that increase access to health care services in rural communities.
The legislation addresses challenges faced by rural residents, such as workforce shortages, transportation barriers, facility closures, and gaps in health insurance coverage. These issues contribute to higher unmet health care needs and a 43 percent higher mortality rate among rural Americans compared to those living in urban or suburban areas.
By reauthorizing Rural Health Services Outreach programs, the bill seeks to expand access to preventive screenings and chronic disease management for nearly half a million people who receive direct services from these initiatives each year. The measure also aims to broaden telehealth offerings and reduce emergency department visits.
“Health care outcomes should not depend on a patient’s zip code. However, this is the reality for millions of Americans living in rural communities,” said Rep. Carter. “Rural Health Care Services Outreach Programs address this issue, expanding vitally important health services to reach people in all communities. I thank my colleagues for their support in reauthorizing these critical programs to address the chronic health care needs of rural communities through flexible, community-driven solutions.”
Carter is currently serving as U.S. Representative for Georgia’s 1st district after replacing Jack Kingston in 2015 according to his congressional biography.
In recent elections, Carter has maintained strong support within his district: he defeated Patti Hewitt with 62% of the vote in 2024; Wade Herring with just over 59% in 2022; Joyce Griggs with about 58% in 2020; Lisa Ring with nearly 58% in 2018; and Brian Reese with almost 61% back in the general election of 2014.
